title: I built a trading journal because I kept breaking my own rules
author: swsaputra_
selftext:
![video](g3ryq8csfb0i1 "Red Candle Journal")

I’ve been a programmer for over 15 years, and I’ve traded forex and gold on the side for a little over three. For me, the hardest part has been following my own rules consistently, especially when the market moves fast and I feel like I’m missing a trade.

I’d finish a session knowing I’d gone off-plan, but by the time I reviewed it, I couldn’t always remember what I saw on the chart or why I made that decision. So I built **Red Candle**, a desktop trading journal for people who trade short timeframes, especially scalpers.

Here’s what I use it for:

* **Timeline Chart and Journal** help me put chart screenshots and trade notes in order so I can review a session later.
* **Similar Patterns** finds comparable setups in my imported candle history and shows what happened after each match. I can see whether those past setups continued, reversed, or went sideways.
* **AI Analysis** explains the market structure and nearby support and resistance that the app calculates from my imported candles. It gives me another way to review the chart, while the trading decision stays mine.

I built it to work with local AI through Ollama or LM Studio so trading data used for analysis can stay on your computer. You can also connect a cloud provider with your own API key. If you choose cloud AI, the data used for that analysis is sent to the provider.

I’m offering **10 people 30 days of free access**, with no card required. I’d especially like to hear from people who trade alongside a day job. If you’re interested, send me a DM with what you trade and how you review your trades today.

And if you’ve tried keeping a trading journal before, **what made you stick with it or stop using it?** That’s the feedback I’d most like to hear.

Red Candle is available for macOS. [redcandle.tech](https://redcandle.tech/)
